body.name: \((I_{\pi}:\pi\in\Pi_m)\)
body.construction: If \(N<b_{\beta,D}\log(40m)\), set \(I_\pi=G_\tau\) for every \(\pi\).  Otherwise use \(T^{\mathrm{ci}}_{n,m}=\{N/\log(40m)\}^{1/(2\beta+4)}\).  At \(z=T^{\mathrm{ci}}_{n,m},eT^{\mathrm{ci}}_{n,m}\), form \(J_{xa}(z)=[0,1]\cap2m\operatorname{CP}_{\gamma_0/(4m)}\{K_{xa}(z);n\}\).  Let the raw region be the intersection of \([1,4]\times[-\log2,0]\) with the two induced Hall strips displayed in the symbol definition of \(\Theta_{xa}\).  If this raw region is nonempty, set \(\Theta_{xa}\) equal to it; if it is empty, set \(\Theta_{xa}:=\{(1,-\log2)\}\).  For each \(\pi\), minimize and maximize the unique core root over \(\prod_x\Theta_{x,\pi(x)}\), obtaining \(\underline t_\pi\) and \(\overline t_\pi\), and put \(J_\pi^*:=[\underline t_\pi-\varepsilon_\tau,\overline t_\pi+\varepsilon_\tau]\).  If \(J_\pi^*\cap G_\tau\neq\varnothing\), set \(I_\pi:=J_\pi^*\cap G_\tau\).  If the intersection is empty, set \(I_\pi\) equal to the singleton containing the metric projection of the midpoint of \(J_\pi^*\) onto \(G_\tau\).  Compact polygon optimization, finite policy enumeration, and monotone scalar bisection make every endpoint computable.  On the simultaneous count-coverage event every raw region is nonempty and contains its true Hall-core parameter, and every final intersection is nonempty and contains the true log policy value; hence the two off-event singleton totalizations do not alter the finite-sample coverage proof.  Their lengths are zero, so unlike full-rectangle or global-interval fallbacks they do not obstruct shrinking width in probability.
